title: Regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics and non-perturbative renormalization of the shear viscosity of incompressible fluids
authors: Mattis Harhoff, Cedric Riedel, Johannes Roth, Sören Schlichting
abstract: We propose a regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics that preserves all relevant symmetries. By considering an incompressible fluid, we demonstrate explicitly that the regularized theory is UV finite, and therefore admits a continuum limit. Strikingly, the regularized theory of stochastic fluid dynamics is not only amenable to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory, but also to functional methods in the continuum. We exploit this to perform renormalization group improved perturbative calculations of the renormalization of the shear viscosity of an incompressible fluid in two and three spatial dimensions, and compare our results to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory.
summary: This work develops a mathematically consistent regularization scheme for stochastic fluid dynamics, allowing for the calculation of transport properties like shear viscosity. By treating the system as an Effective Field Theory, the authors use renormalization group techniques to calculate the viscosity, successfully bridging the gap between continuum field theory and numerical lattice simulations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics to ensure the theory is UV finite and admits a well-defined continuum limit for calculating transport coefficients.
main_result: The authors successfully perform renormalization group improved perturbative calculations of the shear viscosity ($\eta$) in 2D and 3D, showing agreement between continuum field theory and lattice simulations.
method: The approach involves proposing a symmetry-preserving regularization scheme for the stochastic Navier-Stokes equations, followed by applying functional methods like the Martin-Siggia-Rose-Janssen-De Dominicis formalism for renormalization group analysis.
model_or_system: The system is an incompressible fluid whose dynamics are governed by stochastic Navier-Stokes equations, treated as an Effective Field Theory (EFT) matching a microscopic quantum field theory.
key_observables: Shear viscosity ($\eta$), renormalized viscosity ($\eta_R$), and the stationary probability distribution $p_{eq}[\vec{\pi}]$.
important_parameters: UV cutoff ($\Lambda$), lattice spacing ($a$), and the inverse thermal Reynolds number ($Re^{-1}_\Lambda$).
main_assumptions: The theory relies on the validity of the Poisson bracket formalism and assumes that the proposed regularization scheme correctly preserves all relevant symmetries and fluctuation-dissipation relations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the EFT structure with a cutoff separating microscopic (UV) and macroscopic (IR) scales, and show the dependence of the renormalized viscosity on the cutoff scale in 3D.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the stochastic hydrodynamics formalism, derives the necessary symmetries and conservation laws, develops the regularization scheme, performs the RG calculations for $\eta$, and finally compares the continuum results with lattice simulations.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluid dynamics, the rigorous application of EFT techniques, renormalization group flow, and the need to reconcile continuum limits with lattice discretizations are highly relevant methodologies used in analyzing open quantum systems and many-body dynamics.
